ground_truth.description: The rewrite of `_fail_n_pass_n1` replaces the original 'else → return pass' branch (explicitly named 'N+1 (re-merged, no N) → pass') with `raise AssertionError`. The original test deliberately supported the case where N+1 is re-verified alone after N failed and expected it to pass. If the speculative worker re-verifies N+1 after discarding N (the standard discard-and-retry flow), the patched verification function now raises AssertionError instead of returning a passing result, causing the test to error/behave differently rather than exercise the intended path. This is the most likely cause of the unexpected escalation despite review passing.

The `filterwarnings = ["error:..."]` entries are set at the project-wide `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` level, so unawaited-coroutine and sync-test-in-asyncio-class warnings become hard errors for the entire suite, not just merge_queue tests. Any pre-existing test elsewhere that legitimately leaks a coroutine or has a sync test in an `@pytest.mark.asyncio` class will now fail; only the test_steward class split addresses one such case.

task.title: Fix AsyncMock setup in merge_queue verification tests
task.description:
orchestrator/tests/test_merge_queue.py emits RuntimeWarning 'coroutine AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call was never awaited' at merge_queue.py:280 and 987 for several tests (test_verify_failure_returns_blocked, test_speculative_discard_on_failure, test_speculative_events_emitted, test_verifier_remerge_exception_releases_slot, test_speculative_chain_invalidation_propagates, test_speculative_remerge_preserves_duration_ms, test_verify_failure).

Root cause: test sets `mock_verify = AsyncMock()` then `mock_verify.return_value.passed = False`. Accessing `.return_value` on an AsyncMock creates an AsyncMock child and configures it, so when the mock is awaited, an unnecessary coroutine is created and discarded. The suggested fix is `AsyncMock(return_value=SimpleNamespace(passed=False, summary='tests failed'))` or `AsyncMock(return_value=MagicMock(passed=False))`.

Also test_steward.py:1009 test_timeout_counts_dict_initialized_empty is decorated with @pytest.mark.asyncio but is a sync function — fix by removing the asyncio mark from that specific test.

These are test-hygiene issues, not production bugs, but the warnings clutter CI output and mask genuine resource leaks.
